messages:
ashok: Putting a design note here: "priority windows" for trace capture. Goal: limit long-tail ingestion by keeping high-fidelity only inside short recent windows per route, plus on-demand rehydration. Wanted feedback on data-path and UX.

kelly: Quick Q: priority window = time duration per-route where we keep full traces?

ashok: Exactly. Examples: routes with high QPS get sliding window = 5m full-fidelity, older data becomes compact. Windows expand/contract based on recent error budget and query replays.

noah: How do we handle expensive joins for billing if most originals are compacted?

ashok: Compact envelopes keep a minimal join header: hashed_billing_key, tenant_hint, route_fingerprint, provenance_token. Billing pipeline uses probabilistic join + small reservoir of full traces for calibration. We emit per-aggregation "confidence" and "reservoir_sample_rate".

fern: What about SRE alerts and latency histograms that rely on full spans? If window shrinks we lose granularity.

ashok: Two mitigations: (1) preserve a tiny directional histogram wire format inside compact envelope (approx quantiles), (2) allow route-level opt-outs for critical alerts where window stays long. Also a migration doc for teams.

kelly: Rollout plan? We need dry-run first.

ashok: Dry-run: mark traces with bucket tags but ingest full payloads for 7 days, then run the compacting job offline to estimate cost vs analytic loss. Metrics: per-route cost_delta, attr_conflict_rate, alert_breakage_index.

noah: Rehydration latency expectations? On-demand may hit cold storage. Need SLA for customer-facing queries.

ashok: Target rehydrate_p95 < 2s for common routes (if within recent hot window historic store can rehydrate faster), otherwise fallback to best-effort with confidence flag. We will add a Console indicator "rehydration_latency_est".

fern: Console UX: teams need to see route window size, confidence, reservoir_rate and a one-click request to increase window for troubleshooting.

obs-bot: Created task OBS-1420: "priority-windowing + rehydration follow-up" with subtasks: dry-run-sim, compact-envelope-schema, rehydrate-api, console-prototype.

kelly: Edge vs proxy? Prefer proxy for rollout control.

ashok: Agreed. We'll prototype as sidecar/proxy first so ops can toggle per-cluster. Next steps: ashok writes RFC update with schema & math, kelly runs dry-run script, noah drafts Console mocks, fern prepares migration checklist. Ping here for syncs.

ashok: Thanks all, keeping momentum.
